fields.label: the Scald floor
fields.description: The floor beneath the Scald: scalding vents and boiling mats under the water. Not yet surveyed in detail.

fields.label: Grey Sea floor
fields.description: The floor beneath Grey Sea: a salt-white floor of pillars and brine pools. Not yet surveyed in detail.

fields.label: Twilight Sea floor
fields.description: The floor beneath Twilight Sea: a dim floor lit by what lives on it. Not yet surveyed in detail.

fields.label: Chill floor
fields.description: The floor beneath Chill: the cold garden at the bottom of the crater lake. Not yet surveyed in detail.

fields.label: bottom-walker
fields.description: A domed, heat-glossed giant that walks the Scald's floor on a hundred short thick legs, head low, scraping the rainbow mats off the bottom in slow broad swathes. It is the muddal's far larger kin and unmistakably the same make. It barely notices anything the size of a person; it is simply very large and has somewhere to be. Where it grazes, the mats' pigment-rich underside is left briefly bare.

fields.label: glasskelle
fields.description: Hard-soft coral that builds its skeleton from the silica the vents dissolve, drawing glass thread out of water no colony should survive. Its tissue lives inside fused glass capillaries laid down at vent temperature, so the boil reads as pleasantly cool. It cannot live off a vent. When a colony dies it stays standing: a vent field is a forest of clear dead spires with living colour only at the growing tips.

fields.label: pulsebead
fields.description: Between geyser pulses a pulsebead is a dead ceramic pea baked onto the stone. When the splash comes it wakes, swells into a soft grey-green button, feeds and seeds, and bakes back to a bead as the stone dries. Pilgrims call a blooming field "the applause."

fields.label: scald vent
fields.description: A shore-side vent of the Scald's own breath — high-pressure steam venting on its own rhythm. A condenser raised here drinks the clean breath for free; a geothermal generator will not recognize it as its own kind of geyser.

fields.label: coolant manifold
fields.description: A broken annular manifold, half sunk in the crater floor. Five pipe runs leave it, each ending in a capped service outlet with a gauge port. This is the Rust Cathedral's old return gallery: the place its coolant came back from the Scald. Some runs are dead. At least one still pulls warm water home.

fields.label: coolant outlet
fields.description: The capped end of a coolant run, with a gauge port. A colonist can hook a gauge to it and read what the run is doing: its pressure along its length, the water's temperature, and which way it flows.

fields.label: coolant pipe
fields.description: A run of corroded coolant pipe lying along the floor, sound enough to follow.

fields.label: burst coolant pipe
fields.description: A pipe segment split open along its length. Whatever this run carried stopped here.

fields.label: service locker
fields.description: A sealed engineer's locker set into the manifold's housing. Its latch is driven by the return circuit: it will only release once the live return has been identified.

fields.label: immersion-engineering schematic
fields.description: Corroded plates of engineer's drawings: how to keep a sealed hull livable while it sits in hot water, as the Rust Cathedral's own crews did. What it unlocks is not wired yet (SCALD_GALLERY_SCHEMATIC_UNLOCK_1).

fields.label: Cathedral heat-dump log
fields.description: A service log of where the Rust Cathedral vented its waste heat after the collapse. Every entry names the Scald: it re-tapped the crater lake as a coolant sink, dumping heat where a boiling sea makes more heat invisible, and its captured outflow is the Rustwave.

fields.label: comb ice-rock
fields.description: Water-ice bedrock, pale and squared by something that was not weather. It is one tine of a horseshoe wider than a village, and the horseshoe is only the part of a larger thing that stands above the floor.

fields.label: black busbar
fields.description: A slab of black conductor cut straight through the ice and out of sight in both directions. It hums at the edge of hearing. Where it leaves the horseshoe it runs on beneath the floor, past the edge of the map, toward machinery nobody here has seen the end of.

fields.label: inspection stud
fields.description: A capped test stud set into the inner rim of the junction, where an engineer once clipped a meter to read the current going home. Overhead, the drowned aurora makes its glass cap flicker in no pattern a person has worked out. This is the return junction of the planet's unfinished dynamo; nobody here controls it, and nothing here answers back.
